description.narrative: Integrated Approach Programme on Fostering Food Security and Resilience in 7 States in Sub-Saharan regions in Northern Nigeria. GEF funded project

sector.narrative: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

description.narrative: Number of additional people (smallholder farmers) benefitting from strengthened livelihoods through solutions for management of natural resources, ecosystems services, chemicals and waste

comment.narrative: About 35 million people are threatened by desertification and land degradation in the project area, with more than 50% food insecure

(i) Organise workshops to establish effective advocacy platforms that will influence NSFSRF (ii) Establish agroforestry system to increase vegetation cover and carbon stored in trees in project communities (iii) Support out-grower arrangement between beneficiaries and agricultural private sectors (iv) Develop practical sustainable intensification on rice and groundnut Production & Processing (TOT ) of 5,000 youths and 2,000 women across the 70 project communities (v)Procure inputs (seedlings, protective materiasl for seedlings, source of water etc) for establishing agroforestry system

(i) the establishment of multistakeholder gender sensitive and inclusive advocacy platform at both national and state levels. The platform members comprises of 33 members (Male =27, Female = 6) drawn from from other platforms like voices for food security (VFS), association of small scale agro producers in Nigeria (ASSPIN) and grow Africa amongst others with track records of commitment and substantial work experience in Food and Nutrition Security activities. (ii) finalization and submission of the reviewed and harmonized relevant agricultural policies to the Federal Ministry of Agriculture for their adoption and use. (ii) Socio-economic and physical features of the 70 project communities updated on the vital signs platform.

(i)Support the government to evaluate the performance of relevant national and state level institution in various sectors food (ii). Draft a National Food and Nutrition Security Policy (NFNSP) and National System for Food Nutrition Security (NSFNS) (iii). Train beneficiaries on viability and benefits of suitable crops and sustainable agricultural practices identified in 2019 (iv). Consultancy payment to establish demonstration plots of rice and groundnut as well as other community suitable crops to display viability and benefits of climate smart agricultural practices. (v). Consultancy payment to develop practical sustainable intensification on rice and groundnut Production & Processing (TOT ) of 5,000 youths and 2,000 women across the 70 project communities

(i). The project supported and trained beneficiaries with a starter pack for alternative livelihood in bee keeping, ram & goat fattening and dairy goat. The total number of the beneficiaries in this category are 1,389 (Male = 815, Female = 574) (ii)National food and nutrition security policies and strategies (National Policy on Environment, National Policy on Agriculture, National Food Security Programmes and Policy on Food Nutrition) submitted. (iii). 39,981 (Male = 24,009, Female = 15,972) jobs and improved livelihood in both on-farm and off-farm activities (iv)Training of beneficiaries on identified community suitable crops and sustainable agricultural practices (GAP) A total number of 6,102 (Male = 3,023, Female = 3,079) community beneficiaries attended and started putting what they learned into practice during this ongoing rainy season.

(i) Construct 4 solar-powered storage systems in 2 States (ii) Conduct a sustainability and dip stick assessment of women and youth involvement in value chain of rice and groundnut (iii) Support technical trainings and field-visits within and outside the country for national and state level officers and subject matter expert

Project has handled climate change and food security successfully, and has far exceeded its achievements at the middle line. The achievements include smart agriculture, drought control, sustainable livelihood, bee keeping and honey production amongst other strategies has improved the income of farmers and made them happy resulting in the success of the project.
